title: Does The Job (edited)
text:
Does The Job (edited). Heater warms up quick, heat output is rather impressive and warms my 12-foot x 12-foot bedroom in just a few minutes. There was a brief smell as it initially started up but that was even shorter than I expected. The timer and remote, which is fairly basic, work fine. Setting a temperature allows the heater to turn on and off over time maintaining the room temperature. I like that a unit at this price point has a removable and washable filter. I gave it four stars because we can't award half stars, this is really more a three and a half star item because of the. . .
Cons -
The display is on the top, the unit uses the same beep tone for everything. So you can't see temperature or any changes you make to the system. I wake up in the middle of the night, it's chilly and I want the room warmer so I grab the remote, there's a couple beeps and. . . I have NO idea if I've changed the fan, temperature, turned the swing mode on. You need to get up and look at top of the unit to see what's what.
The temperature only changes in five (5) degree increments. Why? I like specific comfort levels and it's really hard, for me at least, to be comfortable at 75° when I want it to be 72° and 60° is too chilly when I would prefer 63°. It may be nit picky but I see no reason in 2020 for a heater to only operate at five degree intervals.
I have no idea what the swing feature does. The unit doesn't pivot and it only has one exhaust vent so. . . what's it do? The instruction book doesn't say.
(here's the edit) Found another con, this is enough to drop the rating to three stars. I don't like my room hot, warm is more than enough. I'm quite happy to have the temp set to 60° or if it's a bit damp and raw 65°. Turn the unit off, as an example, when you're going out and don't want to leave a heater running when you aren't home and it defaults to 70° when you turn it back on! That just. . . annoying! Who makes these arbitrary decisions and why? This is dumb. Especially since the manual says it starts up with the previously used settings. It does not. (end edit)
The unit operates either vertically or horizontally so there's no tip-over protection.
